summary.oneLiner: SCHIL is a Fast-Moving Consumer Healthcare (FMCH) company in India built on legacy self-care brands (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA), combining pharmaceutical-grade scientific trust with consumer-retail distribution reach.
summary.business: Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India Limited (SCHIL) manufactures and sells pharmaceutical/consumer-healthcare (drugs and pharmaceuticals) products under a Fast-Moving Consumer Healthcare model that combines the scientific trust of healthcare with the speed and reach of consumer retail. It distributes through wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce platforms across India, and in 2025 commenced export operations, adding an international dimension to its growth.

currentContext.strengths: Portfolio of category-leading, decades-trusted OTC/self-care brands (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA) with established consumer recall|Strong distribution network spanning wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce platforms|Backed by Sanofi/Opella global consumer-healthcare heritage of scientific rigour, evidence-based formulations and quality standards|Renewed, focused marketing and demand-generation investment behind legacy brands for the first time in over a decade, re-establishing consumer and HCP engagement
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the core brand portfolio (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA) through disciplined, focused marketing and demand-generation investment|Expand access across channels and geographies, including scaling the nascent export business|Accelerate digital and future-ready capabilities, including AI-enabled insights for faster, better-informed decisions|Run a synergistic demand-generation model integrating Healthcare Professional (HCP) recommendation, consumer engagement and retail availability|Simplify the organisation ('radically simple') by streamlining decision-making and processes to enhance agility|Continue innovation agenda with science-backed product launches (e.g. Allegra-D) addressing targeted consumer needs|Leverage the scale and innovation capabilities of parent Opella Healthcare to support growth|The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 75 per equity share (face value Rs 10) for the Financial Year ended 31st December 2025, placed for shareholder approval at the AGM; no other multi-year dividend/buyback/debt-reduction policy is stated in this bundle.
currentContext.expansion: No new plant, site or manufacturing-capacity expansion is disclosed; the Company reports no owned manufacturing plants (BRSR shows 0 plants nationally/internationally, only 1 national office), consistent with a toll-manufacturing/outsourced production model. The stated expansion during the year was commercial and geographic rather than industrial: the Company commenced export operations in 2025, adding an international dimension to its distribution footprint, and continued to expand its FMCH distribution network (wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce) and invest in 'future-ready' digital systems.
currentContext.mdna: Consumer behaviour is shifting from reactive treatment-led consumption towards preventive and lifestyle-oriented healthcare spending|Large under-penetration in consumer healthcare categories in India (an estimated 70-80% of the population Vitamin D deficient, 30-40% with allergy-related conditions) with low awareness/treatment levels is seen as a growth opportunity|Rising health awareness, increasing self-care adoption, improving disposable incomes and growth in nutraceuticals/dietary supplements support industry demand|Digital platforms and e-commerce are expanding accessibility and product penetration into Tier II and Tier III markets|Evolving OTC regulatory framework, pricing pressures and increasing competitive intensity (from pharma, FMCG and digital-first wellness brands) are expected to shape the sector|Raw material cost volatility, regulatory scrutiny and product standardisation requirements remain industry headwinds|Export portfolio is gaining momentum, expanding geographic footprint and diversifying the business beyond India

risks.note: Following Sanofi's global sale of its consumer healthcare business, Opal Bidco SAS (majority voting control held by the Clayton, Dubilier & Rice Group) now exercises ultimate indirect control over the Company, and a mandatory open offer to public shareholders was triggered under SEBI SAST Regulations.

The CFO role changed hands twice during the year: Ms. Maithilee Mistry (Whole-time Director & CFO) resigned effective 5th May 2025; Mr. Narahari Naidu was appointed CFO effective 4th August 2025 and resigned effective 15th October 2025; Mr. Richard D'souza was then appointed CFO effective 16th October 2025.

Geopolitical tensions (West Asia, Russia-Ukraine), evolving tariffs and trade regulations have raised procurement and freight costs and caused cargo delays and supply disruptions for businesses dependent on imported inputs and cross-border sourcing.

risks.risk: Raw material cost volatility and regulatory scrutiny
risks.note: The consumer healthcare industry faces raw material cost volatility, regulatory scrutiny and product standardisation requirements, which can pressure margins and compliance costs.
Increasing participation by pharmaceutical companies, FMCG players and digital-first wellness brands is intensifying competition across product categories and distribution channels.

Business performance is linked to Indian consumer demand and disposable-income trends, which are influenced by inflation (CPI reaching 3.4% as of March 2026) and broader macroeconomic and global-trade conditions.

one-line thesis: Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India is transforming from a legacy pharma division into a high-growth FMCH leader by reinvesting in brand equity, consumer education, and digital-first demand generation, leveraging its top-tier portfolio and India-first autonomy to capture rising self-medication trends. Profitable growth is being driven by doubling HCP reach, expanding retail access, and AI-enabled marketing, with OTC regulation as a key near-term catalyst.
financial scorecard: rev:+21% YoY; EBITDA:+13% YoY; PAT:+33% YoY; orderbook:N/A; netdebt:N/A
guidance: No forward-looking guidance provided; management emphasized growth and penetration as core focus with profitable trajectory.
segment / subsidiary detail: Allergy (Allegra #3 by value); Pain (Combiflam #5); Vitamin D (DePURA #5); VMS (emerging). All brands are market leaders in volume or value within their categories. No new segment launches yet, but category expansion under evaluation.
growth verticals / optionality: Pipeline includes potential new launches from Opella global R&D (e.g., Allegra D as precedent); exploration of gastro/enterogermina/laxatives categories; crowdsourced innovation initiatives underway; potential product transfers from parent entity under board review.
margins & cost dynamics: Operating margin at 37%; ANP investment increased from low single-digit to mid-teens; supply chain fully localized in India, reducing dependency on global inputs and improving cost control.
capex / expansion: Not explicitly disclosed; implied investments in digital infrastructure, AI tools, retail displays, and field force enablement.
capital allocation: Prioritizing A&P spend (mid-teens % of revenue), HCP engagement, retail visibility, talent acquisition, and AI/digital tech. No dividends or buybacks mentioned; all capital directed toward growth levers.
risks & watch-items: Delayed OTC regulation; recall recurrence; execution risk in doubling HCP/reach; competition from local players; reliance on FMCH talent retention; potential channel conflict with indirect distributors.
management quality / tone: Highly confident, energetic, and transformational. Management emphasizes empowerment, agility, challenger mindset, and India-first autonomy. Strong focus on culture, diversity, and accountability. Open to innovation and external models (e.g., 3rd party reps) if cost-effective.
non-obvious takeaways: Despite minimal past marketing, legacy brands (Avil, Combiflam) retain top market positions — indicating immense latent brand equity. B-Corp certification is rare in Indian FMCH and signals long-term ESG credibility. AI is already generating creatives in-house — a first for an Indian pharma subsidiary.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
